content: 1. For men aged 19–30 years, the recommended daily intake of magnesium is 400 mg/day. For women in the same age group, it is 310 mg/day. Pregnant women aged ≤50 years should consume 350 mg/day, while breastfeeding women aged ≤50 years should consume 310 mg/day. 2. For men aged >30 years, the recommended daily intake of magnesium increases to 420 mg/day. For women in this age group, it is 320 mg/day. Pregnant women aged ≤50 years should consume 360 mg/day, and breastfeeding women aged ≤50 years should consume 320 mg/day. 3. Magnesium citrate can be administered orally in a single daily dose of 195–300 mL or in divided doses, accompanied by a full glass of water. Alternatively, 2–4 tablets can be taken orally at bedtime, or 1 tablet twice daily, as directed by a healthcare provider. The product should be refrigerated to maintain its potency and palatability. 4. The safety and efficacy of magnesium citrate have not been established for children under 2 years of age. For children aged 2–6 years, the recommended dose is 60–90 mL orally, either as a single dose or in divided doses, not exceeding 90 mL in 24 hours. For children aged 6–12 years, the dose is 90–210 mL, taken as a single dose or in divided doses with a full glass of water. For individuals aged >12 years, the dose is 195–300 mL orally, either as a single daily dose or in divided doses with a full glass of water. 5. Magnesium citrate decreases the levels or effects of baloxavir marboxil by binding to cations in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract, which reduces absorption. It is recommended to avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Studies in monkeys have shown that concurrent use with calcium, aluminum, or iron significantly decreases plasma levels of baloxavir. Human studies have not been conducted. 6. Magnesium citrate reduces the levels of demeclocycline by inhibiting its absorption in the GI tract. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 7. Magnesium citrate decreases the levels or effects of dolutegravir by binding to cations in the GI tract. To minimize this interaction, dolutegravir should be administered 2 hours before or 6 hours after taking medications containing polyvalent cations. 8. Magnesium citrate reduces the levels of doxycycline by inhibiting its absorption in the GI tract. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Magnesium citrate decreases the levels of eltrombopag by inhibiting its absorption in the GI tract. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated, and the two drugs should be separated by at least 4 hours. 10. Magnesium citrate reduces the levels of minocycline by inhibiting its absorption in the GI tract. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Magnesium citrate decreases the levels of oxytetracycline by inhibiting its absorption in the GI tract. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 12. Magnesium citrate reduces the effects of intravenous potassium phosphates by binding to cations in the GI tract. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Magnesium also decreases serum phosphate concentrations by binding dietary phosphate. Alternatives should be used if available. 13. Magnesium citrate decreases the levels of tetracycline by inhibiting its absorption in the GI tract. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Magnesium citrate reduces the levels or effects of bictegravir by binding to cations in the GI tract. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Bictegravir can be taken under fasting conditions 2 hours before antacids containing aluminum, magnesium, or calcium. Routine administration of bictegravir simultaneously with, or 2 hours after, such antacids is not recommended. 15. Magnesium citrate decreases the levels or effects of cabotegravir by binding to cations in the GI tract. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Polyvalent cation products should be administered at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after taking oral cabotegravir. 16. Magnesium citrate reduces the levels of ciprofloxacin by inhibiting its absorption in the GI tract. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration of ciprofloxacin with multivalent cation-containing products may reduce ciprofloxacin bioavailability by up to 90%. Ciprofloxacin should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after using these products. Alternatives should be used if available. 17. Magnesium citrate decreases the levels of deflazacort by shifting magnesium from the blood to tissue storage. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Magnesium citrate reduces the levels of fleroxacin by inhibiting its absorption in the GI tract. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 19. Magnesium citrate decreases the levels of gemifloxacin by inhibiting its absorption in the GI tract. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 20. Magnesium citrate and ifosfamide may increase each other’s toxicity through nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring of electrolytes and renal function is recommended.
